text:
Marathon Petroleum stock rose 0.69% today to close at $424.89, continuing a strong two-week rally that's gained 9.59% overall. The company has benefited from a tight global oil market: U.S. crude is trading at $107 per barrel while world oil prices sit at $130.80—a $23.80-per-barrel spread that reflects Middle East supply disruptions (Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline shutdown, Iranian tensions, Houthi attacks) creating real scarcity. U.S. refineries are running at 96.8% capacity, meaning Marathon can process crude at near maximum rates to capture profits from this wide price gap.

The rally reflects what refiners call the "crack spread"—the difference between the price they pay for crude and the price they receive for finished fuel like gasoline and diesel. When global crude prices spike (as they have amid Middle East unrest) while U.S. crude lags behind due to temporary supply relief and diplomatic talk, refiners in America profit from buying cheaper local oil and selling into a world market paying far more. Gasoline and diesel storage levels remain moderate (207.7 million and 107.9 million barrels respectively), suggesting steady demand is draining supplies, which supports fuel prices.
